---
title: "Stacked column"
description: "Summarize compositional abundance across samples or groups with stacked-column graphics."
---

## Purpose

The stacked-column utility is suited to composition-style data such as taxonomic categories, functional categories, pathway classes or other features whose contributions should be compared across samples.

## Recommended workflow

1. Prepare a table with explicit sample/group labels, category labels and numeric values.
2. Decide whether values should represent absolute abundance or proportions.
3. Aggregate rare categories into `Other` when a long legend would obscure the signal.
4. Generate the stacked-column plot.
5. Check that the category order and sample order support the biological comparison.
6. Export the underlying summarized table together with the figure.

::: {.callout-tip}
For relative-abundance plots, verify that each sample sums to the intended denominator after filtering. Removing categories before renormalization changes the apparent proportions.
:::
